program_overview.title: Abitur Mathematik in English: Leistungskurs and Grundkurs
program_overview.tagline: Analysis, Analytische Geometrie and Stochastik for the Abitur, live and in English, with a mentor who matches your pace and accent and explains every step clearly.
program_overview.description:
This is a live online maths course for students in the gymnasiale Oberstufe in Germany preparing for the Abitur in Mathematik, at Leistungskurs (erhöhtes Anforderungsniveau) or Grundkurs (grundlegendes Anforderungsniveau) level. It covers the three areas of the written exam: Analysis, Analytische Geometrie or Lineare Algebra, and Stochastik, plus the exam technique for the part without aids and the part with aids.

Classes are live and taught in English only. The mentor matches each student's pace and accent: speaks clearly, slows down through long derivations, rephrases and checks understanding. A student whose first language is German gets Abitur maths help and English practice in the same class, which helps with English-language degrees and maths texts later. We never teach in German, but every worksheet puts the German term beside the English one (Ableitung and derivative, Wendepunkt and point of inflection, Zufallsgröße and random variable), so the work maps straight onto school notes and the exam paper.

The course is built on the format of the common Länder task pool. The IQB, which coordinates the pools, says that since the 2017 exam year the Länder have had common Abitur task pools in German, maths, English and French, and each Land's own commission decides which pool tasks it uses and how far it adds its own. The IQB describes the maths exam as two parts: in Part A no aids are allowed, and in Part B aids may be used, with Analysis, Analytische Geometrie or Lineare Algebra, and Stochastik in both. Part A must be handed in within the first 110 minutes at raised level and the first 100 minutes at basic level. The raised-level exam is worth 100 Bewertungseinheiten with "Die Arbeitszeit einschließlich Auswahlzeit beträgt 300 Minuten", and the basic-level exam 80 Bewertungseinheiten in 255 minutes. In NRW, for example, the 2027 written maths Abitur for LK and GK is on Wednesday 5 May 2027.

Every practice problem and mock paper in this course is our own, written in the pool format. After each exam year the IQB publishes the pool tasks the Länder used, with expectations and marking notes, and students can work those themselves; we never copy them into our materials. Topics, aids and rules differ by Land, so the mentor maps the course to the student's Land in the first class. We are independent of the IQB and every Land ministry and make no promise of grades.

learning_path.phase_1: Analysis: functions, derivatives and curve analysis, exponential functions, integrals and areas, and modelling with functions
learning_path.phase_2: Analytische Geometrie and Lineare Algebra: vectors, lines and planes, positions, distances and angles, and matrices where the Land requires them
learning_path.phase_3: Stochastik and exam craft: probability, binomial and normal distributions, hypothesis tests, then timed Part A and Part B practice and full mocks

career_outcomes: Secure Analysis, Geometrie and Stochastik for the written Abitur
Fast, accurate work without aids for Part A
Confident use of the permitted calculator or CAS for Part B
Clear written reasoning that follows the exam's operators
A strong base for maths, science, engineering or economics degrees
Mathematical English for study and work abroad

phase_1_analysis.title: PHASE 1: Analysis (Months 1-2, Weeks 1-8)
phase_1_analysis.description: The largest area of the written exam, from derivatives and curve analysis to integrals and modelling.

month_1_derivatives.title: Month 1: Functions, Derivatives and Curve Analysis

week_1_2.title: Weeks 1-2: Your Exam, Your Pace, and Derivatives
topics: A diagnostic: your Land, phase, LK or GK, permitted aids and what your class is doing now
How we work in English: the mentor's pace, phrases for asking to repeat, and a German to English maths term list
The structure of the pool exam: Part A without aids, Part B with aids, and the time limits
Polynomial functions, symmetry and behaviour at infinity
The derivative as a rate of change and the slope of a tangent
Power, sum, product, quotient and chain rules
projects: A personal formula sheet with German and English names, built and checked in class
week_1_2.practice: Short no-aids derivative drills of our own after each class

week_3_4.title: Weeks 3-4: Curve Analysis (Kurvendiskussion)
topics: Zeros, extreme points and points of inflection, with necessary and sufficient conditions
Monotony and curvature from the first and second derivatives
Tangents and normals at a point
Reading the graph of f from the graph of f′ and the reverse
Function families with a parameter
Writing each step in the language of the operators (bestimmen, nachweisen, begründen)
projects: A complete curve analysis of a function family, written up as an exam answer
week_3_4.practice: Original curve analysis tasks with and without aids
week_3_4.assessment: Month 1 check: a timed no-aids set plus one longer Part B style task

month_2_exponentials_integrals.title: Month 2: Exponential Functions, Integrals and Modelling

week_5_6.title: Weeks 5-6: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
topics: The natural exponential function and its derivative
Natural logarithms and solving exponential equations
Growth and decay models, and limited growth
Composite functions of e, such as x times e to the minus x
Leistungskurs depth: more complex function families and proofs
Interpreting a model's result in context, in full sentences
projects: A growth model for a real data set, fitted and interpreted
week_5_6.practice: Original modelling tasks with exponential functions

week_7_8.title: Weeks 7-8: Integrals and Areas
topics: Antiderivatives and the fundamental theorem of calculus
Definite integrals and the area under a curve and between curves
Integration by substitution and by parts (as your Land requires)
Reconstructing a quantity from a rate of change
Average values and improper integrals for the Leistungskurs
Mixed Analysis tasks in the pool style
projects: A full Analysis task of our own, solved, then rewritten after feedback
week_7_8.practice: Timed mixed Analysis practice in Part A and Part B style
week_7_8.assessment: Phase 1 assessment: a timed Analysis paper of original problems, Part A and Part B

phase_2_geometry_linear_algebra.title: PHASE 2: Analytische Geometrie and Lineare Algebra (Months 3-4, Weeks 9-16)
phase_2_geometry_linear_algebra.description: Vectors in space, lines and planes, and the matrix topics some Länder examine.

week_9_10.title: Weeks 9-10: Vectors and Lines
topics: Points and vectors in three-dimensional space
Vector addition, scalar multiplication and linear combinations
The scalar product, lengths and angles
Parametric equations of lines
Positions of two lines: parallel, identical, intersecting or skew
Sketching 3D situations clearly by hand
projects: A geometry pack of our own based on a pyramid or a roof

week_11_12.title: Weeks 11-12: Planes
topics: Parametric, normal and coordinate forms of a plane
Converting between forms and the cross product
Intersection of a line and a plane, and of two planes
Positions of planes and lines
Modelling a real object with planes
Explaining a geometric method in clear English
projects: A model of a building's roof faces with all intersections computed
week_11_12.practice: Original plane tasks with and without aids
week_11_12.assessment: Month 3 check: a timed geometry set

week_13_14.title: Weeks 13-14: Distances and Angles
topics: Distance from a point to a plane and the Hesse normal form
Distance from a point to a line and between skew lines (LK)
Angles between lines, between planes, and between a line and a plane
Reflections and orthogonal projections
Mixed geometry problems with parameters
Checking answers for plausibility with a sketch
projects: A full geometry task of our own, solved and rewritten after feedback
week_13_14.practice: Timed geometry practice in Part A and Part B style

week_15_16.title: Weeks 15-16: Matrices and Systems of Equations
topics: Linear systems and the Gaussian elimination method
Solution sets: unique, none or infinitely many
Matrices and matrix multiplication where the Land examines them
Transition matrices and processes over several steps
Choosing which Lineare Algebra topics your Land requires
Explaining a matrix model in context
projects: A transition-matrix model for a population or market share
week_15_16.assessment: Phase 2 assessment: a timed Geometrie and Lineare Algebra paper of original problems

phase_3_stochastics_and_exam.title: PHASE 3: Stochastik and Exam Craft (Months 5-6, Weeks 17-24)
phase_3_stochastics_and_exam.description: Probability and statistics for the third area of the exam, then full timed practice in the pool format.

week_17_18.title: Weeks 17-18: Probability and the Binomial Distribution
topics: Tree diagrams, path rules and conditional probability
Four-field tables and independence
Random variables, expected value and standard deviation
Bernoulli chains and the binomial distribution
Cumulative probabilities with the permitted aid
Writing the random variable and its distribution clearly before calculating
projects: A probability investigation of a game of our own design

week_19_20.title: Weeks 19-20: Normal Distribution and Hypothesis Tests
topics: The normal distribution and the bell curve, where your Land includes it
Approximating the binomial distribution
One-sided and two-sided hypothesis tests
Significance level, decision rule and the two types of error
Leistungskurs depth: confidence intervals and test planning
Interpreting a test result in context, in full sentences
projects: A test planned and run on a claim from a product or poll of our own
week_19_20.practice: Original Stochastik tasks with and without aids
week_19_20.assessment: Month 5 check: a timed Stochastik paper

month_6_exam_craft.title: Month 6: Abitur Exam Craft and Full Mocks

week_21_22.title: Weeks 21-22: Part A, Part B and the Operators
topics: Part A without aids: speed, accuracy and choosing tasks in the time allowed
Part B with aids: using the permitted calculator or CAS efficiently and writing the steps
The general competences in the KMK standards, from Mathematisch argumentieren (K1) to Mathematisch modellieren (K3) and beyond
Operators in maths tasks and what each one asks for
Choosing tasks during the Auswahlzeit
Error log review across all three areas
projects: A personal exam strategy sheet, tested on a timed half paper
week_21_22.practice: Timed Part A sets and Part B tasks of our own

week_23_24.title: Weeks 23-24: Full Mock Papers and Final Plan
topics: A full mock of our own: 300 minutes for LK or 255 minutes for GK, including choice time
Detailed written feedback in the style of an expectation horizon
Oral exam practice for students with maths as an oral subject
Targeted repair of the weakest topics
A revision plan to your Land's exam date
Calm routines for the exam day
projects: Two full timed mocks with written feedback
week_23_24.practice: Full timed papers of original problems
week_23_24.assessment: Final assessment: a full timed mock of original problems in the pool format

faqs.question: What is the Abitur Mathematik in English course?
faqs.answer: A live online course for Oberstufe students in Germany, roughly ages 16 to 19, preparing for the maths Abitur at Leistungskurs or Grundkurs level. It covers Analysis, Analytische Geometrie or Lineare Algebra, and Stochastik, plus exam technique for the parts with and without aids. It runs for 24 weeks with 2 live classes a week, taught in English.

faqs.question: Are the classes in German or in English?
faqs.answer: English only. We never teach in German. The mentor matches your pace and accent: speaks clearly, slows down through long calculations, rephrases and checks understanding. Many students see this as a plus, because they get Abitur maths help and English practice at once. Every worksheet puts the German term beside the English one, so the maths maps onto your school notes and exam paper.

faqs.question: How is the written maths Abitur structured?
faqs.answer: For tasks from the common pool, the IQB describes two parts: Part A without aids and Part B with aids, both covering Analysis, Analytische Geometrie or Lineare Algebra, and Stochastik. Part A must be handed in within the first 110 minutes at raised level and 100 minutes at basic level. The raised-level exam is worth 100 Bewertungseinheiten in 300 minutes and the basic-level exam 80 in 255 minutes, both including choice time. Each Land decides which pool tasks it uses and may add its own.

faqs.question: Is the course for Leistungskurs or Grundkurs?
faqs.answer: Both. The Grundkurs path covers the core of all three areas, and the Leistungskurs path adds depth such as more complex function families, distances between skew lines and confidence intervals. Full mocks are timed at 300 minutes for LK and 255 minutes for GK.

faqs.question: When is the maths Abitur in 2027?
faqs.answer: It depends on your Land. The IQB says that since 2022 the maths exams have been held largely on common dates across Länder. In NRW the written maths Abitur for LK and GK is on Wednesday 5 May 2027. Check your own Land's ministry or school for your date.

faqs.question: Do you use real Abitur tasks?
faqs.answer: No. Every problem and mock in the course is our own, written in the pool format. The IQB publishes the pool tasks the Länder used after each exam year, with expectations and marking notes, and students can work through those themselves. We never copy them into our materials.

faqs.question: Which calculator or CAS should I use?
faqs.answer: The one your Land and school permit for Part B. We practise with whichever aid you are allowed. KMK notes that new common rules on digital aids apply from the 2030 Abitur, so students taking the Abitur later should check their Land's rules.

faqs.question: My English is not strong. Will I keep up?
faqs.answer: Maths is mostly symbols, and the mentor slows down, repeats and rephrases whenever you ask. Many students find the maths vocabulary in English quick to learn when it sits beside the German term on every worksheet. The free first class shows you whether the pace suits you.

faqs.question: When are classes, with the time difference to India?
faqs.answer: Timing is flexible on weekdays or weekends: choose a batch, or 1-on-1 at your convenience. Our teachers work in India time, which is 4 hours 30 minutes ahead of Germany in winter and 3 hours 30 minutes ahead in summer, so German afternoon, early evening and weekend slots are realistic.

faqs.question: Do you promise a grade?
faqs.answer: No. We promise careful teaching, honest feedback and regular timed practice. We are independent of the IQB and every Land ministry, and our certificate is not an Abitur grade or German qualification.

faqs.question: Can I try a class first?
faqs.answer: Yes. The first class is a free demo, so you can hear the mentor's pace and decide with no pressure.
